questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to find a good job after leaving university
Why so many young teachers leave their jobs each year
Whether teenagers at school should have part-time jobs
How much money teenagers spend on clothes at weekends
questions.why: Neil says the topic is 'Should schoolchildren have jobs?'

questions.q: What was Dan's first ever job?
options: Delivering newspapers at 14
Teaching English
Stacking shelves in a supermarket
Working in a fish and chip shop
questions.why: Dan says he had a paper round when he was 14.

questions.q: What does the first teenager do in their job?
options: Cooks burgers and chips for customers in a cafe
Tidies the shelves and helps customers find things
Delivers newspapers to houses early in the morning
Works at the till taking money from customers
questions.why: The teenager says they make the shelves look organised and show customers where products are.

questions.q: How much does the second teenager usually work?
options: Only on Saturday mornings, for about six hours
Four hours a week, always on Sunday afternoons
Only during the long summer school holidays
About nine hours, on school nights and weekends
questions.why: They work nine hours a week: two school nights, plus Saturday and Sunday.

questions.q: What does the BBC report say about work permits for children?
options: They are no longer needed
The number rose to 30,000 in 2016
The number fell from nearly 30,000 to 23,000
Most were given for TV and modelling work
questions.why: The report says permits fell from nearly 30,000 in 2012 to just 23,000 in 2016.

questions.q: What conflict does the report describe?
options: Teenagers want jobs but most shops won't hire anyone under 18
Employers want experience, but teens are pushed to focus on study
Parents want teens to work, but schools refuse to give permits
Teens earn too much money and then stop studying for exams
questions.why: Employers bemoan young people's lack of experience, but teens face pressure to concentrate on studies.

questions.q: What does Neil think about his own teenage jobs?
options: They harmed his school results and his exam grades
They were boring and taught him nothing useful at all
He wishes he had spent that time studying more instead
They taught him about working with adults and handling money
questions.why: Neil says his jobs taught him lessons about working with adults and managing his money.

questions.q: What did Dan learn from his paper round?
options: The value of hard work
How to talk to customers
That he wanted to be a teacher
How to save money
questions.why: Dan says his paper round taught him the value of hard work and didn't hinder him.
